title: How to make cursor bigger in Cursor on Mac: a guide for better visibility
metaTitle: How to make cursor bigger in Cursor on Mac
description: Learn how to make the cursor bigger in Cursor on Mac by adjusting your system accessibility settings, as the editor uses your macOS pointer configuration.
intro: To make your cursor bigger in Cursor on your Mac, you must adjust the system-wide pointer settings in macOS. Cursor inherits its mouse pointer configuration directly from your operating system, so there is no internal setting within the editor to change the size of your cursor.
tldr: Open System Settings on your Mac.
Navigate to Accessibility and then Display.
Cursor will automatically update to reflect your new system pointer size.

blocks.text: Many developers find that the default cursor size on high-resolution displays can be difficult to track, especially when working in a dense environment like the Cursor IDE. Because Cursor is a fork of VS Code, it relies on the underlying macOS framework for handling input devices, including your mouse and trackpad. This means that any adjustments you make to your system pointer will apply to Cursor instantly.
Adjusting your system pointer size

The most effective way to make your cursor easier to see is to modify the global macOS settings. This change is not limited to the Cursor app; it will affect your cursor across every application you use on your Mac. If you only want a larger cursor while coding, you can always revert these changes after your session.

items: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Click on Accessibility in the sidebar.
Select Display from the list of options on the right.
Drag the Pointer size slider to the right to increase the size of the cursor.
Observe the changes in real time as you move the slider.

blocks.text: After you adjust this slider, the change should take effect immediately. If you have Cursor open in the background, you will notice the pointer size update as soon as you hover over the editor window. You do not need to restart the application for the system-wide change to take effect.
Using the Shake to Locate feature

If you do not want to keep a large cursor at all times, macOS offers a clever feature called Shake to Locate. When this is enabled, the cursor will temporarily grow in size when you move your mouse or trackpad quickly back and forth. This is a common strategy for developers who prefer a standard cursor size for precision but often lose track of it on large or multiple monitors.

To enable this, return to the same Accessibility > Display menu in your System Settings. Look for the toggle labeled Shake mouse pointer to locate and ensure it is turned on. Once active, a quick flick of your hand will make the cursor grow significantly, allowing you to find its position on the screen within a fraction of a second.
Customizing pointer colors for better contrast

Sometimes the issue is not the size of the cursor, but its visibility against the dark background of the Cursor IDE. In the same Accessibility > Display menu, you can modify the Pointer outline color and the Pointer fill color. Choosing a high-contrast color for the outline can make a significant difference in how easily you can track the cursor while reading through complex code blocks.

If you use a dark theme in Cursor, a bright white or light blue outline is often the most effective choice. Experiment with these settings to see which color combination provides the best feedback during long coding sessions.
Distinguishing between cursor size and UI scaling

It is quite common for users to confuse the size of the mouse pointer with the size of the text and UI elements. If you find that the entire interface is too small, changing the cursor size will not solve your problem. Instead, you should adjust the zoom level of the Cursor IDE itself.

You can increase the zoom level by pressing Command (⌘) + + on your keyboard. To zoom out, press Command (⌘) + -. This will scale the font, the sidebar, and the chat panels, making the entire workspace more readable. This setting is specific to the Cursor IDE and will not affect other applications on your Mac.
Common mistakes and troubleshooting

One common mistake is attempting to edit the internal CSS files of the Cursor app to force a custom cursor size. While this is technically possible, it is discouraged. Modifying the core files of the editor can lead to stability issues. You may see a warning indicating that your Cursor installation appears to be corrupt. This is usually a false positive, but it is an unnecessary headache that you can avoid by sticking to the system-wide settings.

If the cursor size does not seem to change after you have adjusted the system settings, try closing and reopening the Cursor application. While macOS usually applies these changes globally and instantly, an active app process might occasionally cache the previous pointer state. A simple restart forces the app to re-initialize its windowing environment with the updated system parameters.
Why Cursor uses system settings

Cursor is designed to feel like a native macOS application. By deferring to the operating system for accessibility settings, it ensures that your experience remains consistent. If you have already configured your Mac to work well for your specific visual needs, Cursor will respect those configurations without requiring extra manual setup.

This approach also helps with performance. Because the system manages the pointer rendering, Cursor does not need to consume extra resources to manage its own custom cursor implementation. This keeps the editor fast and responsive, which is essential when working with large codebases or heavy AI-assisted tasks.
What to do next

Once you have your cursor size set to a comfortable level, you might want to look into other ways to improve your workflow in Cursor. Many users who adjust their pointer settings also find it helpful to customize their font sizes or keyboard shortcuts. If you are struggling with the AI chat panel, you can try adjusting the zoom level as mentioned earlier to make the text more readable.

Remember that Cursor is updated very frequently. If you find that certain AI features are difficult to interact with, check the official changelog on their website. They often add new settings that might address your concerns without requiring you to modify system files or use third-party tools.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor size only for Cursor and not for other apps?
faq.answer: No. Because Cursor uses the standard macOS pointer system, any change you make to the pointer size will apply to every application on your Mac.

faq.question: Does Cursor have an internal setting for cursor size?
faq.answer: No, Cursor does not have a native setting for changing the mouse pointer size. It relies entirely on the macOS system settings.

faq.question: Why does my Cursor installation show as corrupt?
faq.answer: If you have manually modified the internal CSS files of the Cursor app, the editor may detect the change and flag the installation as corrupt. Reinstalling the app usually fixes this.

faq.question: How do I make the text in Cursor bigger?
faq.answer: You can zoom in on the interface by pressing Command (⌘) + + on your keyboard. This will increase the size of the text and UI elements.
